title: Is it time to find a side hustle?
description:
More and more of us are picking up side hustles - US national employment data shows that the number of people with more than one job is going up year on year, and a survey found that the majority of them are 16-24 year olds. So why are more of us turning to side hustles? And what’s the best way to start one?

We hear from Katie (@katiesgarms), Vera (@viavera_) and Shania (@shaniasvault) who have all started successful side hustles. They share how they got into them and their top tips for getting started. And Chelsea Coates from the What in the World team explains why the current global job market is encouraging more people to pick up second jobs - and the things to look out for if you’re thinking of doing this.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討副業日益普及的趨勢與經營技巧。節目邀請 Katie、Vera 與 Shaniyah 三位來賓，分享她們經營二手衣拍賣、服裝紙樣設計及數位行銷等副業的經驗。BBC 團隊記者 Chelsea Coates 指出，調查顯示高達 55% 的副業從業者為 16 至 24 歲的 Z 世代青年。面對全球青年失業率上升、入門職缺減少與生活成本增加，越來越多人透過兼職尋求財務穩定與彈性。節目最後建議，嘗試副業時應先檢查正職合約是否包含利益衝突條款，並設定務實目標、善用現有資源。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores the growing popularity of side hustles, particularly among young adults. Guests Katie, Vera, and Shaniyah share how they turned passions—such as reselling clothes, designing sewing patterns, and digital marketing—into rewarding secondary income streams. BBC video journalist Chelsea Coates highlights that 55% of side hustlers are aged 16 to 24, driven by high global youth unemployment, automated entry-level positions, and rising cost-of-living pressures. The episode offers practical guidance for prospective side hustlers, emphasizing the importance of checking workplace contracts for conflict-of-interest clauses, setting realistic goals, and utilizing existing tools to get started.
